previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in epistaxis and right knee pain. She landed face-first and on her right knee, causing a nasal bleed controlled with anterior-posterior packing and a vertically oriented, minimally displaced patellar fracture identified on CT. Arthrocentesis removed 110cc of blood from a large suprapatellar effusion, and the knee was immobilized in a brace for non-operative management. Her platelet count, previously 10,000 during a recent admission for AVNRT-related syncope, was 103,000 on admission but downtrended to 67,000; aspirin was held and heparin initiated for DVT prophylaxis per hematologist guidance. The nasal tampon was removed without rebleeding. She remained stable with no arrhythmias, and her chronic diastolic heart failure was managed with continued medications. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehab with orthopedic follow-up in two weeks, ongoing platelet monitoring, and cardiology follow-up for pending EP evaluation.

FINDINGS:  There is subsegmental atelectasis at the imaged lung bases
associated with areas of scarring.  The imaged portion of the heart is normal

possibly the aortic valve.  Suture material is noted along the
gastroesophageal junction.

adrenal glands is normal.  The pancreas is atrophic.  The right kidney is

lesion in the interpolar region measuring approximately 12 mm, indeterminate. 
The abdominal aorta is tortuous, though not aneurysmal.  Pattern of aortic
calcification is abnormal in this patient with known dissection extending into
the abdominal aorta likely accounting for the pattern of intraluminal
calcification.  There is no retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy or hematoma.

The stomach beyond the suture plane appears unremarkable.  The duodenum is
normal.

PELVIS:  Small bowel is non-dilated.  There is diffuse dilation of the colon
without associated obstruction or significant distal impaction.  The bowel
